title: OpenAI starts merging ChatGPT Chat and Work into one usage limit; new Business sign-ups by Nov 30 get 2x usage and fast mode

kept.claim: New ChatGPT Business customers who sign up by Nov 30 get 2x included usage and fast mode at no extra cost for all seats through Dec 31.
kept.evidence: [0] pricing page banner: "Sign up for ChatGPT Business by Nov 30 and get 2x included usage and fast mode at no extra cost for all seats through Dec 31." [2] says OpenAI's pricing page lists an offer for new Business customers: sign up by Nov. 30, get double the included usage and fast mode for all seats through Dec. 31.

kept.claim: OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page.
kept.evidence: [1] says OpenAI plans to bring shared usage limits more broadly in December, per its support page. [2] says the change applies to Plus, Pro and Business starting in December 2026.

kept.claim: Most users are not expected to have to wait for usage resets more often, but a small fraction of the heaviest users may hit limits sooner.
kept.evidence: [1] spokesperson: most users not expected to face more frequent usage resets; a small fraction of heaviest users may hit limits sooner. [2] says OpenAI expects most users won't need to wait for reset more often, and notes heavy users of agent tasks and Codex draw from one pool.

kept.claim: Conversations with the Instant model stay unlimited and do not count toward the shared allowance.
kept.evidence: [1] says Instant conversations remain unlimited and won't count toward the shared allowance, and users can keep using Instant after exhausting limits. [2] says Instant chat will not draw from the shared allowance.

kept.claim: Timing caveat: the Business offer was already on OpenAI's pricing page when fetched (retrieved 2026-11-27) and the offer deadline of Nov 30 is stated by the primary source. The merger announcement predates the Nov 25 TechCrunch story, and the primary OpenAI help-center article could not be fetched (tool limit), so merger claims lack a primary source here.
kept.evidence: [0] pricing banner with Nov 30 and Dec 31 dates. [1] refers to an earlier emailed announcement and to OpenAI's support page for the December plan.

dropped.claim: OpenAI will have Chat and Work share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, per an OpenAI spokesperson.
dropped.evidence: [1] "Under the new system, Chat and Work will share a single usage meter across ChatGPT, the OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch." [2] describes a shared allowance across ChatGPT and Codex as Work's agentic capabilities come into main ChatGPT, but does not say Chat and Work share one meter in these words. [0] does not state it (it says "Usage refers to Chat limits"). The OpenAI help-center page cited by both articles could not be fetched, so there is no primary confirmation.

dropped.claim: OpenAI began rolling out the unified Chat and Work experience to a small group of Pro subscribers, per a Tuesday post on X by product lead Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux.
dropped.evidence: [1] says the update began for a small group of Pro subscribers, as Sottiaux said in an X post on Tuesday. [2] only says a small group of users (not specifically Pro) may see the change before December.

dropped.claim: The merger of Chat and Work was announced earlier than this rollout, in an email to users (the link in TechCrunch points to a Nov 2, 2026 TechCrunch story, which was not fetched).
dropped.evidence: [1] says the rollout follows OpenAI's "earlier announcement" of the merger in an email to users. The date is inferred from the linked URL only.

dropped.claim: The shared allowance applies to Plus, Pro and Business plans and also covers Codex (TechCity's framing).
dropped.evidence: [2] "ChatGPT usage limits on the Plus, Pro and Business plans will become one shared allowance that also covers Codex." [1] does not mention Codex or specific plans in this context (it only mentions Pro for the early rollout).

dropped.claim: Usage under the shared allowance will be counted in tokens, so advanced models and complex tasks use more of it.
dropped.evidence: [2] says usage is measured in tokens and that advanced models and complex tasks use up more. [1] does not say this.

dropped.claim: When users run out, they can wait for the reset, upgrade their plan or buy credits; remaining allowance and reset time appear under Settings > Usage.
dropped.evidence: [2] lists the three options and says the Settings, then Usage page shows combined remaining allowance and reset time. [1] does not state this. [0] only says Enterprise and Business can purchase credits for more access.

dropped.claim: Some subscribers have criticized the merger, fearing less access to advanced reasoning models at the same subscription price.
dropped.evidence: [1] says users raised concerns on social media and OpenAI's community forum that merged limits could leave them with less access to advanced reasoning models while paying the same fees.

dropped.claim: Details still unknown as of Nov 26, 2026: the exact December date for most accounts, how many tokens each plan includes, and what credits cost.
dropped.evidence: [2] "What we don't know yet" section lists these three items.
